title: session-record v1
description: THE FLEET RECORD (remote plan R10): the record the hub's engine STORES for one session, keyed by sessionId and filed with the device the session runs on: the fields core/ownership.json gives to the engine and does not mark derived, and nothing else. The fields of the node that runs the session (owner node: what only that machine observes - projectCwd, lastSeen, lastTool, spawnedAt) are the binding record, schema/session-binding.v1, written only on that device; a local session is the same split with both writers on one machine. LAYOUT (lifecycle store H1): the hub keeps its fleet records as <HordeHome>\store\sessions\fleet\<sessionId>.json, and a node its binding records as <HordeHome>\store\sessions\binding\<sessionId>.json, so a local session's two files never share a name; the hub's read-only mirror of a node's binding records is R13's. A field another owner holds (agent, host, session) lives in that owner's store, and a derived field is computed when it is read; a stored copy of either would be a second writer, which step 0.6 forbids. Values are plain and typed: the engine writes facts it knows, and a field it has not set is absent - never an empty string, -1 or null standing in for 'none'; where wezfleet writes one of those, reading it translates it to absent, as each field below says. ON DISK: one file per session, named by its sessionId (wezfleet's registry names each record the same way: 31 of 31 on 2026-09-30); a reader refuses a record whose schemaVersion is not 1 rather than reading it as this version; and a later version migrates v1 records by writing each as a new whole record, never by editing a v1 file in place into a shape v1 does not describe. These, and 'a label implies a labelCycle', are the WRITER'S RULES: core/Schema.ps1 implements no dependencies or file-name check, so this schema cannot state them. ('labelCycle is never negative' was one too, until core/Schema.ps1 gained minimum; the schema now states it.) No step of planning/migration-plan.html owns that writer yet - Phases 0 to 2 write nothing, and Phase 5 moves writers behind the contract without naming this one - so the step that takes it inherits these rules. x-horde-read gives each field's read order until its switch as store and field only: the store guards and per-read 'when' clauses of core/ownership.json are omitted here, and the table is where they are read. No stored field is marked provisional in the table, and this record has no way to carry that mark, so the test fails if one ever is. The answer-per-field VIEW of a session, over every owner, with unknowns, provenance and provisional marks, is a separate schema, session-view, deferred to step 2.3 where `horde status --json` produces it; the review's findings about value types and answer consistency (the tristate form) apply to that view, not to this record. test/test-schema-session-record.ps1 computes the field list from the ownership table and fails if the two ever differ.

sessionId.description: THE KEY, not a stored fact: the agent's own conversation id, which names this record. The agent owns it (core/ownership.json); the engine only files the record under it. Same shape as schema/pane-session.v1's session_id.

device.description: WHERE THE SESSION RUNS, not a fact of the session and not part of its key (the key is sessionId; engines K1 makes it the harness and id): the device id of the machine the session runs on (core/Device.ps1, remote plan R7), written by the hub's engine when it files the record. Required, because a record that does not say where its session runs cannot be matched with that machine's binding record. Not a row of core/ownership.json until remote plan R13 puts device in the session view. Same shape as schema/node-manifest.v1's deviceId: a lower-case UUID, random, never a host name.

role.description: core/roles.json's native roles. The old vocabulary (master, orchestrator, session) is translated through core/roles.json's aliases when wezfleet is read, and is never stored.

parent.description: The parent session's sessionId: an edge by identity, never by label. Every one of 20 parents in wezfleet's registry is a session id (census 2026-09-30).

label.description: The short handle: an orchestrator's letter alone (one or two capitals, wezfleet Test-WfLooksLikeOrchestratorLetter), or a subsession's letter and its number within that letter - one to four digits, as wezfleet Split-WfLabel reads it (lib/Allocator.ps1:45), never with a leading zero, because New-WfSessionLabel issues numbers from 1. Recycles by design, so it is a handle, never identity. 17 of 17 labels in the registry have this shape (census 2026-09-30).

origin.description: Who opened the session: fleet when the spawner gave it a fleet session id, else user. The only two values Write-WfSessionRecord writes; registry census 2026-09-30: fleet 7, user 24.

fleetSessionId.x-horde-read: W1 fleetSessionId, then W2 fleetSessionId, then W4 sessions[].id, then W3 sessions[].id, then W8 wezfleetSessionId
fleetSessionId.description: The id the run manifest gave this session. wezfleet writes an empty string for none, which translates to absent here: registry census 2026-09-30, present in 31 of 31 records - empty in 24, set in 7 - and absent from none.

retired.description: A tombstone: the session was closed out. Its record is kept so its label stays held (wezfleet Set-WfSessionFields -Retired).

runId.description: The run the session belongs to: yyyyMMdd-HHmmss and a slug (wezfleet New-WfRunId, ConvertTo-WfSlug). 194 of 194 run folders have this shape (census 2026-09-30; the one other folder under a runs directory, handoffs, holds notes and no run.json).

labelCycle.description: Which wrap of the label counter issued the label, so a label resolves to one session. Stored whenever label is, and only then. TRANSLATION FROM WEZFLEET: a labelled record with no labelCycle is stored as 0, the cycle wezfleet itself reads it as (Get-WfLabelState, lib/Allocator.ps1:69-74, 'a record with no labelCycle predates the field and counts as cycle 0'); -1, which wezfleet's spawn claims write for none, and a missing labelCycle on an unlabelled record are absent. Census 2026-09-30: labelCycle is present in 14 of 31 registry records, all 0, and missing from 3 of the 17 labelled ones; 4 of 7 spawn claims carry -1, each with an empty label, and 3 carry neither. Never negative: minimum 0, so -1 is refused here and never stored. 'Stored whenever label is' is the writer's rule (see the top of this schema): core/Schema.ps1 implements no dependencies keyword.

retiredAt.description: When the session was retired, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, as lastSeen.

title.description: The run manifest's title for the session; the manifest defaults it to the session's fleet id (wezfleet lib/Run.ps1).

dependsOn.description: The fleet session ids this session waits for, as the manifest lists them. An empty list is a fact (it waits for none); absent means not recorded. Roster census 2026-09-30: all 422 entries have dependsOn; 381 list none, and the 49 ids the others list are all non-empty strings.
